title: How a pharmacy reports naloxone doses under Board Policy 2024-01
rule_summary: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2024-01: Naloxone Dispensing (adopted 1/11/24, revised 2/6/25) states that, as required by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19B, each Massachusetts pharmacy must report the number of naloxone doses dispensed, and its section II sets out how. The preferred method for a pharmacy to report naloxone dispensing information is with its daily Prescription Monitoring Program (PMP) submissions; the submission of naloxone to the PMP is for data collection purposes only and will not appear on a patient's PMP profile. If the pharmacy chooses not to report naloxone dispensing through the PMP, annually, by January 15, the pharmacy must submit the report by email to the Department address the policy gives, including the following information for the previous calendar year: the name and zip code of the pharmacy; the total number of naloxone doses (not number of prescriptions or manufacturer-supplied units) dispensed; and the total number of those doses paid for with insurance. While not required for the annual report, pharmacies are encouraged also to submit information for each dispensing event that includes the number of doses dispensed, the date dispensed, the zip code of residence for the individual to whom the naloxone is dispensed, and whether the naloxone was paid for with insurance.
exam_relevance: Tests who makes the naloxone dose report under the Board's policy, the preferred route through daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions, the January 15 date and required contents of the emailed annual report for a pharmacy that does not report through the PMP, the counting of doses rather than prescriptions or manufacturer-supplied units, and the difference between required and encouraged content.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2024-01: Naloxone Dispensing (adopted 1/11/24, revised 2/6/25)

numeric_facts.fact: date by which a pharmacy that does not report naloxone dispensing through the PMP must submit its emailed annual report
numeric_facts.conditions: annually, giving the required information for the previous calendar year

exceptions: The emailed annual report due by January 15 is required of a pharmacy that chooses not to report naloxone dispensing through its daily Prescription Monitoring Program submissions.
common_confusions: Counting prescriptions or manufacturer-supplied units instead of naloxone doses.
Assuming that naloxone reported through the Prescription Monitoring Program appears on the patient's PMP profile.
Treating the per-dispensing-event details as required content of the annual report, when the policy encourages them.
